Soojin — initial sizing notes below. I ran the numbers against our typical token-per-GPU throughput for the LLM class they demoed. This is a conservative committed pool to meet p95 and burst headroom.

Proposal (pilot baseline):
- Hardware: 4x A100-80GB (or equivalent 80GB-class q8/Q4f config).
- Expected steady throughput: ~25–40 rps aggregate depending on batching; burst headroom ~65 rps for short windows with pipeline autoscaling.
- Token capacity: ~300–350M tokens/month with modest batching and prefix caching.
- Estimated p95 generation latency: 220–320ms (region network factors assumed)
- Queueing: maintain 20% buffer to avoid p99 spikes — requires 1 extra node for redundancy

Ops notes:
- We recommend colocated pools: SG primary, SYD failover slice (2+2 split) to keep latency for both cities below target.
- No cross-border cache persistence: set cache policy to region-local KV and replicate only model binaries.
- SLA: offer 99% uptime for dedicated tranche; start with 3-month commit and 30% optional burst credit.

Attachments: I put a quick cost sketch + node mapping in the shared drive. Need Marissa on pricing and Lauren to confirm quota availability for new APAC tranche.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — that aligns with our playbook. A couple of practical constraints and a recommended alternative:

Constraints:
- APAC capacity pipeline: we currently have limited A100-80GB headroom in SG for March; we can reassign from a non-critical reserve but that triggers a 2-week provisioning lead.
- Procurement asks for contract cover + price today; pricing for committed 3-month tranche is sensitive to start date.

Recommended approach (to speed to market):
1) Short-term bridge: 2x A100-80GB dedicated in SG + 2x on our reserved burst pool (dedicated warm standby) — this reduces provisioning time and meets initial p95.
2) Parallel capacity commit: provision remaining 2x A100 as a purchase order to arrive by Apr 1; show customer the MA P with a staged ramp (diagram in drive).
3) Network/peering: get Anna to confirm ASN + peering IPs; we can prioritize route optimizations to shave 40–60ms of tail latency.

Pricing ask for Lauren: please approve a 3-month committed quote with optional 30% burst credit and mixed billing (base commit + burst overage at X% discount). I will own the rollout ops and post-deployment monitoring scope.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Capacity & Field Ops, Redwood Inference
